findings.title: Global unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url for every email
findings.body: The new unsubscribe_link string interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}. Email::MessageBuilder renders this key whenever add_unsubscribe_link is true, but it does not provide a default unsubscribe_url. Any mailer or plugin that passes add_unsubscribe_link: true without also passing unsubscribe_url will now raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument while building the email, so the email is not sent. This PR only updates the notification mailer and one spec, so the contract break is easy to miss.

findings.title: unsubscribe assumes a TopicUser row exists and can raise NoMethodError
findings.body: The action does TopicUser.find_by(...) and immediately reads tu.notification_level. For any logged-in user who has no topic_users row for that topic, tu is nil and the request raises NoMethodError, returning a 500. Email recipients usually have a row because send_notification_email calls TopicUser.change, but the route is accessible to any logged-in user, e.g. via a forwarded email or manual URL. Using TopicUser.change would upsert the row; it would also update notifications_changed_at/reason and publish the MessageBus notification_level_change event that direct save! currently bypasses.

findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe endpoint is a GET with no CSRF protection
findings.body: GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe changes the current user's notification_level using only the session cookie. A malicious page can embed this URL as an image or link and, for a logged-in user who can see the topic, silently downgrade or mute the user's subscription. Email link scanners can trigger the same state change. The link needs an unguessable per-user token or the mutation needs to be a POST protected by CSRF.

findings.title: New per-topic unsubscribe behavior has no meaningful test coverage
findings.body: The spec change only adds unsubscribe_url to an existing builder so it no longer exercises the missing-interpolation path. There is no assertion that the new URL appears in the rendered body or HTML, no controller test for creating/muting a TopicUser, no test for the nil-TopicUser case, and no test for Topic#unsubscribe_url. These omissions leave the 500 on missing TopicUser and the global unsubscribe_link interpolation requirement unguarded.
